posts.title: The Bishop of Durham Attempts to Surrender the City, by Susanna Clarke
posts.description: After the real disappointment of Clarke's The Wood at Midwinter (I reviewed it here on Nov.1, 2024), in which a short story is bloated to produce a small overpriced book, I suppose I was forewarned. Yes, The Bishop of Durham Attempts to Surrender the City is very much along the same lines, but the story is a bit more substantial and interesting. posts.title: Pale Grey Idol, issue zero, edited by Michael Kelly
posts.description: This is issue zero of a new magazine, to debut with issue one in early 2027. A slim paperback of 97 pages, it contains six stories-- "Strange Stories of the Ineffable" as the subtitle describes them. posts.title: Votive Offerings, edited by Robert Morgan
posts.description: Robert Morgan has edited some six previous anthologies for his own Sarob Press. This one contains four stories, by four authors, Mark Valentine, John Howard, Peter Bell and Colin Insole. The first three authors are in many of Morgan's previous anthologies, while I think Insole has appeared in only one other Sarob book.
